models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light and benign overnight at Santa Marina; leave for Portorosa at 06:00 to beat a thundery, unsettled afternoon.
briefing.synopsis: A weak, slack pressure pattern sits over the Aeolians - nothing in the data resembles an organised gradient, with consensus winds across all islands running 3-9 kt through tonight and tomorrow. Direction is the story rather than strength: SE around 120° this evening at Salina (7.0 kt, gusting 15.2, ECMWF IFS 18Z / AIFS and ICON-2i 00Z consensus), backing SSW overnight, then swinging NNW by 06:00 tomorrow and staying in the NW-N quadrant through the middle of the day. Thunderstorms are flagged in the 08:00-14:00 period for the Salina-Portorosa corridor, and seas build slowly behind it - Salina wave heights go from 0.7 ft tonight to 1.8 ft tomorrow afternoon and 2.4 ft by Saturday evening.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Porto Santa Marina Salina is the recommendation and scores 0.895 - open to the SSE, but with only about 6 kt in that sector it is a non-issue tonight. Expect 5.5 kt SSW at midnight with an interval-max gust of 19.0 kt, swell 0.3 ft from the west, wave 0.7 ft (ECMWF IFS 18Z / ICON-2i 00Z). Rinella is effectively equivalent at 0.875 if you prefer it; the choice does not matter in this pattern. Only a genuine SSE filling in above the forecast would make it worth shifting round to the lee.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Salina at 06:00: 3.4 kt from the NNW (335°), gust 8.2, wave 0.7 ft - a flat, motoring start. The computed window for Salina to Portorosa is a 06:00 departure for a 10:00 arrival, 3.4 kt NW, 0.7 ft, dead downwind at 166 TWA, which in practice means engines. Conditions are called as deteriorating after 08:00, with thunderstorms flagged in the 08:00-12:00 and 10:00-14:00 windows, so the early start is the whole point; later windows re-open as go at 12:00 and 14:00 but with waves up to 1.9 ft and far wider model spread.

passage_notes.note: All windows graded go. Best of it was the 06:00 slot at 3.5 kt S, 0.7 ft, beam reach; by midday the breeze goes ESE-E at 4-5 kt and you are head to wind - motor. Gusts of 10-13 kt against 4-5 kt means are interval-maxima from a single model in light air, not a squall signal.

Go on the 06:00 departure, 3.4 kt NW, 0.7 ft, running. The 08:00 and 10:00 departures are graded no-go on forecast thunderstorms in the passage window; 12:00 and 14:00 return to go at 4.9-6.9 kt with 1.8-1.9 ft wave. Portorosa Marina on arrival is fully enclosed, scoring 1.0, with 3.9 kt SSE forecast.

cautions: Thunderstorms are in the forecast for the Salina-Portorosa corridor between roughly 08:00 and 14:00 tomorrow. That is the reason for the 06:00 start, and it is the one item worth a radio check before slipping.

Model spread is large around midday and evening tomorrow. At Salina 12:00 the models range from 1.9 to 13.0 kt and at 18:00 from 1.3 to 16.7 kt; off Lipari at 18:00 the spread is 1.9 to 22.7 kt. Treat the consensus figures for tomorrow afternoon as indicative only.

Several large interval-maximum gusts appear in light air - 31.1 kt at Salina 12:00, 36.9 kt at 18:00, 41.4 kt at Filicudi midday. These are maxima over the output interval from a single model, not sustained wind, but in a thundery airmass they are a reminder to keep the main reefed-ready and the awnings down.
Sea state builds steadily after tomorrow: Salina wave 2.0 ft Saturday midnight rising to 2.4 ft Saturday evening, Filicudi to 3.1 ft. Relevant if anyone is planning to extend beyond Portorosa.
briefing.confidence_note: Run-to-run stability is excellent inside 24 hours (mean wind shift 0.5 kt, max 2.5 kt), which supports the overnight and early-morning call, but the models disagree by more than 6 kt from midday tomorrow onward and the thunderstorm risk is inherently low-predictability.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
